## 0. Where Monolist is today (read-only check)
- Settings has a Last.fm row that is designed but not built: `Monolist Player/views/SettingsView.qml:393-418`. Its copy promises browser approval with no password typed in (l.414), a local session key the user can revoke (l.415), and that "a track counts as played once you have heard half of it … Nothing else is sent" (l.416).
  - **Two corrections are needed in l.416.** Last.fm's rule is half the track **or 4 minutes, whichever comes first**, and only for tracks **longer than 30 s**. The app would also send "now playing" updates, which that line doesn't mention.
- The owner still has to decide whether to build Connections: `ROADMAP.md:193`.
- The listening data Monolist already records can't decide a scrobble. `play_events.listened_ms` is "the playhead where the track was left … seeking to the end counts as a full listen" (`src/appdatabase.cpp:130-152`). A scrobbler has to count real playing time.
- Hooks that already exist:
  - an SQLite `settings` key/value table (`appdatabase.cpp:98-101`), which is where a persisted scrobble queue table would naturally go
  - a build-time generated-header pattern that writes to `${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated` (`CMakeLists.txt:68-93`, `cmake/buildinfo.cmake:62`)
  - `build*/` and `CMakeCache.txt` are gitignored (`.gitignore:16-18`)
  - `.env` files are gitignored (`.gitignore:85-88`)
  - the User-Agent is currently `Monolist/0.1` (`src/artworkcache.cpp:207`)
- No Secrets.plist or .env file exists in this tree (checked with a glob, nothing opened).
- The public repo is droidboy08-hub/Monolist (`ROADMAP.md:194`).

## 1. Authentication (official docs)
**Desktop flow** (https://www.last.fm/api/desktopauth):
1. Call `auth.getToken` with `api_key` and `api_sig`. It is signed with the shared secret, so every desktop client has to carry the secret (https://www.last.fm/api/show/auth.getToken).
2. Open `https://www.last.fm/api/auth/?api_key=…&token=…` in the browser. The user approves there.
3. Call `auth.getSession` with `api_key`, `token` and `api_sig`. It returns `name`, `key` (the session key) and `subscriber` (https://www.last.fm/api/show/auth.getSession).
- Tokens are "valid for 60 minutes" and are used once.
- Session keys "have an infinite lifetime by default". Users can revoke them in their Last.fm settings (https://www.last.fm/api/authspec).
- Token errors: 14 means not yet authorised, 15 means expired.

**Web flow with a callback** (https://www.last.fm/api/webauth):
- Send the user to `…/api/auth/?api_key=…&cb=<url>`. Last.fm redirects to `<cb>?token=…`, then you call `auth.getSession`. The `cb` parameter overrides the callback set on the API account.
- Desktop players use this with a loopback server:
  - Strawberry listens on `QHostAddress::LocalHost` and passes `cb=http://localhost:<port>/` (strawberry `src/core/localredirectserver.cpp:55-64`, `src/scrobbler/lastfmscrobbler.cpp:199-214`).
  - Clementine uses the same loopback approach (`src/internet/lastfm/lastfmservice.cpp`, LocalRedirectServer include).
  - Tauon uses the two-button desktop flow instead: "Login" opens the browser, then the user clicks "Done" (Tauon `src/tauon/t_modules/t_main.py:4724-4763`, via pylast SessionKeyGenerator).
  - Pear Desktop (th-ch/youtube-music) uses auth.gettoken and watches the page in its own browser window (`src/plugins/scrobbler/services/lastfm.ts:232-265`).
- RFC 8252 §7.3/§8.3 recommends a loopback redirect for native apps, and the IP literal rather than "localhost" (https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc8252#section-8.5).
- **Untested:** whether Last.fm accepts `cb=http://127.0.0.1:port`. `localhost` is proven to work (Strawberry).

**Avoid `auth.getMobileSession`.** It takes the user's plain-text password over HTTPS POST and is meant for "standalone mobile devices" (https://www.last.fm/api/show/auth.getMobileSession). Sayonara still uses it (`src/Components/Streaming/LastFM/LFMLoginThread.cpp:95-108`), and it contradicts Monolist's own design copy.

## 2. Request signing (api_sig)
- Sort all parameters by name, concatenate them as `<name><value>` (raw UTF-8, not URL-encoded), append the shared secret, and take the MD5 hash (https://www.last.fm/api/authspec, https://www.last.fm/api/desktopauth).
- "You must not include the format and callback parameters" in the signature (authspec).
- For batches, parameters are sorted in ASCII order (https://www.last.fm/api/show/track.scrobble).
- A Qt reference implementation: Strawberry `lastfmscrobbler.cpp:352-377`. It sorts, signs raw name+value, uses `QCryptographicHash::Md5` with lowercase hex, adds `format=json` after signing, and POSTs. That code is GPL and Monolist is MIT, so implement from the spec rather than copying it.
- Endpoint: `https://ws.audioscrobbler.com/2.0/`. Strawberry uses HTTPS (`lastfmscrobbler.cpp:71`); the docs still show http (https://www.last.fm/api/rest).
- Write methods must be POST with every parameter, including `method`, in the body.
- In JSON, errors come back as `{"error":N,"message":…}` (https://www.last.fm/api/rest).
- Last.fm asks for an identifiable User-Agent (https://www.last.fm/api/intro).

## 3. Methods and parameters
**`track.updateNowPlaying`** (POST, needs auth; https://www.last.fm/api/show/track.updateNowPlaying)
- Required: `artist`, `track`, `api_key`, `api_sig`, `sk`.
- Optional: `album`, `trackNumber`, `context`, `mbid`, `duration`, `albumArtist`.
- Send it "as soon as a user starts listening". It does not affect charts (https://www.last.fm/api/scrobbling).

**`track.scrobble`** (POST, needs auth; https://www.last.fm/api/show/track.scrobble)
- Required: `artist[i]`, `track[i]`, `timestamp[i]`, `api_key`, `api_sig`, `sk`. The timestamp is the UNIX time the track **started** playing.
- Optional: `album`, `context`, `streamId`, `chosenByUser`, `trackNumber`, `mbid`, `albumArtist`, `duration`.
- Up to 50 per batch (`[0..49]`). A single scrobble can drop the `[i]`.
- The response gives `accepted`/`ignored` counts. Per-item `ignoredMessage` codes: 1 artist ignored, 2 track ignored, 3 timestamp too old, 4 timestamp too new, 5 daily limit exceeded.
- Send `chosenByUser=0` when the user did not pick the track (radio or recommendations). That applies to Monolist's autoplay and recommender.
- Don't feed now-playing "corrections" back into scrobbles unless the user approved them (https://www.last.fm/api/scrobbling).

## 4. When a track counts as played
- The track must be longer than 30 s.
- It must have been played for at least half its duration or 4 minutes, whichever comes first (https://www.last.fm/api/scrobbling).
- Quod Libet implements exactly this: minimum 30 s, then 50% or 240 s (`quodlibet/ext/events/qlscrobbler.py`).

## 5. Offline queue and ordering
- The docs ask for a persistent local cache that survives restarts. "Scrobbles should be sent in order … cached scrobbles should be sent before new scrobbles", in batches of up to 50 (https://www.last.fm/api/scrobbling).
- How others do it:
  - Strawberry keeps a `lastfmscrobbler.cache` file with 50 per request (`lastfmscrobbler.cpp:74-76, 568`). It marks items as sent, deletes them on success and clears the sent flag on failure (per WebFetch summary of the same file).
  - Quod Libet pickles its queue to `scrobbler_cache_v2` and autosaves every 30 s (qlscrobbler.py).
- A pitfall found in another project (2026): a client deleted its whole queue when it got errors 10, 13 or 26 (bad or suspended key, bad signature), wiping up to 10,000 queued scrobbles in about 200 requests. It also deleted items ignored with code 5 (daily limit). The fix is to keep the queue and pause (https://github.com/jm2/tributary/issues/335).

## 6. Error codes and retry policy
- The full code list is at https://www.last.fm/api/errorcodes. The relevant ones:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 4 | auth failed |
| 6 | invalid parameters |
| 8 | operation failed |
| 9 | invalid session key |
| 10 | invalid API key |
| 11 | service offline |
| 13 | invalid signature |
| 14 / 15 | token not authorised / expired |
| 16 | temporarily unavailable |
| 26 | API key suspended |
| 29 | rate limit exceeded |

- Official guidance (https://www.last.fm/api/scrobbling):
  - Retry on 11 and 16.
  - On 9, re-authenticate first.
  - Treat other errors as malformed requests.
  - "you must inspect the content of the response" whatever the HTTP status.

## 7. Rate and volume limits
- The ToS gives no numbers. §4.4 says Last.fm "sets and enforces limits … (e.g. limiting the number of API requests … or the number of users you may serve)" (https://www.last.fm/api/tos).
- /api/intro warns that accounts making "several calls per second" may be suspended.
- A real error-29 message reads "This application has made too many requests in a short period. If this is your API key, see …tos#4.4" (Navidrome issue, 2023-06-28, https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/issues/2421).
- Community-documented, not in the official docs: about 2,800 scrobbles per user per day, and a 14-day maximum age on timestamps (https://github.com/SHOEGAZEssb/Last.fm-Scrubbler-WPF/blob/master/README.md).
- Secondhand (the Kodi forum page returned 403): Last.fm suspended the XBMC/Kodi key at over 100M calls a day, about 10 times any other key (search result for forum.kodi.tv tid=195597).

## 8. API terms of use (https://www.last.fm/api/tos, no version date on the page)
- §3.1: non-commercial use only; commercial use needs a separate agreement.
- §2.6: Last.fm "will provide You with an API key" (the key is issued to the account holder).
- §2.7: use a "powered by AudioScrobbler" button linking to Last.fm.
- §4.2.2: credit Last.fm when redistributing its data.
- §4.3.4: cache according to HTTP headers; a storage cap of about 100 MB.
- §5.1: no personally identifying or contacting users. Also no use "on any website that … facilitates or condones the illegal or unauthorised use or sharing of content". **Uncertain:** whether this reaches a desktop app that streams YouTube through yt-dlp. It is worded for websites; Pear Desktop and Web Scrobbler scrobble YouTube Music openly. This is a risk for the owner to judge, not legal advice.
- §9.2: termination "at any time … without cause". §9.3: stop using the API and delete Last.fm data.
- **The ToS never uses the words "secret", "confidential" or "credentials"** (checked with a targeted fetch).

## 9. How open-source players handle the key and secret (values deliberately not reproduced)
**Committed in plain text in a public repo:**
- Clementine: `src/internet/lastfm/lastfmservice.cpp:52-53` (`kApiKey`, `kSecret`).
- Rhythmbox: `plugins/audioscrobbler/rb-audioscrobbler-service.c`, in the `/* Last.fm details */` block near the top (about l.35-50; lines reported by WebFetch, not exact). A comment says the key "belongs to Jamie Nicol … generated May 2010".
- Audacious: `src/scrobbler2/scrobbler.h:27-28`.
- Amarok: `src/core/support/Amarok.h:218-219`, used through liblastfm in `src/services/lastfm/LastFmService.cpp:109-110`.
- Tauon: `src/tauon/t_modules/t_main.py:4706,4708`, with `# noqa: S105` to silence the hard-coded-password lint.
- Sayonara: `src/Components/Streaming/LastFM/LFMGlobals.h:30-31`.
- Web Scrobbler: `src/core/scrobbler/lastfm/lastfm-scrobbler.ts:22-29`.
- Cider 1 (AGPL, archived 2024): `src/main/plugins/lastfm.ts:12-15`, web flow with `cb=cider://auth/lastfm` (l.41). Cider 2 is closed source.
- mpris-scrobbler: committed defaults in `meson_options.txt` (`lastfm_api_key`, `lastfm_api_secret`).
- Pear Desktop / th-ch youtube-music (MIT, about 33.6k stars, the closest analogue to Monolist): default key and secret "registered by @semvis123" in `src/plugins/scrobbler/index.ts:56,94-95`. Users can override both in the menu (`menu.ts:26-52`).

**Injected at build time, kept out of git:**
- Strawberry:
  - `cmake/ApiCredentials.cmake` declares `LASTFM_API_KEY` and `LASTFM_SHARED_SECRET` as empty `CACHE STRING`s, set with `-D`. They can optionally be AES-obfuscated as `ENC:iv:ciphertext`.
  - They are written into `src/apicredentials.h.in` with `#cmakedefine`, and read by `lastfmscrobbler.cpp:80-102`.
  - Users can always switch to their own key and secret (`use_custom_api_credentials`, `lastfmscrobbler.cpp:145-147`). Builds without compiled keys force custom credentials.
  - Maintainer's stated reason: forks otherwise "continue to use the same API credentials". The credentials ship only, obfuscated, in the official `.tar.xz` (forum post https://forum.strawberrymusicplayer.org/post/9371).
  - Seen only in a search snippet (post not opened): Strawberry's forum tells users registering their own Last.fm credentials to leave the Callback URL blank.
- Pano Scrobbler (Android): `lastfm.key` and `lastfm.secret` go in an uncommitted `local.properties` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kawaiiDango/pano-scrobbler/main/instructions.md).

**Users paste their own:**
- rescrobbled: config or environment variables `LASTFM_KEY` / `LASTFM_SECRET` (https://github.com/InputUsername/rescrobbled).
- Scrobblr (macOS): "Bring your own Last.fm API key", because a shared key "can be revoked and break the app for everyone" (https://asharahmed.github.io/scrobblr/).
- Navidrome (a server) dropped its shared key in v0.51.0 on 2024-01-21. Operators now set `LastFM.ApiKey` and `LastFM.Secret` (defaults are empty at `conf/configuration.go:1081-1082`; https://github.com/navidrome/navidrome/releases/tag/v0.51.0). The stated reason is behind a Reddit link I couldn't open.

**Built-in default plus an optional override:**
- Music Assistant: "includes the required API credentials", with its own key and secret available in advanced settings (https://www.music-assistant.io/plugins/lastfm_scrobble/).
- Pear Desktop and Strawberry also allow overrides.

**Doesn't talk to Last.fm itself:**
- Feishin relies on the server to scrobble. A client-side Last.fm request was closed as not planned (https://github.com/jeffvli/feishin/issues/1135).
- Quod Libet uses the legacy 1.2 handshake with the username and an MD5 of the password, client id `qlb`, and no API key (qlscrobbler.py).

## 10. What Last.fm says
- **I found no official statement for or against publishing a key or secret in open source.** The ToS and docs don't address it, and I found no staff post saying so.
- What the docs do establish:
  - The secret signs every call, including `auth.getToken`. A desktop client therefore has to ship it; there is no public-client (PKCE-style) flow.
  - The key is issued to the account holder (§2.6).
  - Last.fm can limit "the number of users you may serve" (§4.4), suspend a key (error 26) or terminate (§9.2). The account owner carries that risk.
- The general principle, from RFC 8252 §8.5: secrets "statically included as part of an app distributed to multiple users should not be treated as confidential". Obfuscation only deters casual reuse.
- The Application name entered at registration is shown to users when they connect (https://github.com/owncloud/music/wiki/Setting-up-Last.fm-connection).
- Fields on the create form (the form itself needs a login, so this is second-hand): Contact email, Application name, Application description, Callback URL, Application homepage. Only name and email matter; a callback isn't needed for the desktop or `cb` flows (owncloud wiki; https://github.com/wesback/scrobble-backfill/issues/65; Navidrome docs https://www.navidrome.org/docs/usage/integration/external-services/).
- Keys are listed afterwards at https://www.last.fm/api/accounts.
research.recommendation:
**Recommendation: follow Strawberry's model. Put the credentials in at build time, keep them out of git, and let users paste their own.**

**What to build**
1. **Credentials.**
   - Add CMake cache variables `MONOLIST_LASTFM_API_KEY` and `MONOLIST_LASTFM_SECRET`, empty by default and also readable from same-named environment variables.
   - Have `configure_file` write them to `${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated/apicredentials.h`, next to buildinfo.h (`CMakeLists.txt:68-93`). That folder is under the gitignored `build*/` and `CMakeCache.txt` (`.gitignore:16-18`).
   - Commit only the `.h.in` template, which holds no values.
   - Official Windows and macOS release builds get the values from the owner's own environment or GitHub Actions secrets.
   - Builds with no compiled key show a "Use your own Last.fm API account" option (key and secret fields). Keep that override available in official builds too.
   - Don't write the secret, token or session key to logs. Optionally XOR-obfuscate the compiled strings; don't treat that as real security (RFC 8252 §8.5).
   - Committing the values like Clementine or Pear Desktop is legal and common. It invites forks to reuse the key, and those forks' traffic counts against a key Last.fm can rate-limit or suspend (Navidrome error 29, then shared key removed; Kodi suspension).
   - Asking every user to create an API account (rescrobbled, Navidrome) is poor UX for a consumer player.
2. **Sign-in.**
   - Use the web flow with a loopback callback: a QTcpServer on 127.0.0.1 at a random port, and `cb=http://localhost:<port>/`, which Strawberry proves works (try 127.0.0.1 later). Then call `auth.getSession`.
   - Fall back to the desktop token flow (auth.getToken, open the browser, the user clicks "I've approved it") if the listener can't start.
   - Never use getMobileSession.
   - Store the session key in the app (Windows Credential Manager or the Keychain if you add that for YouTube cookies; otherwise the `settings` table, as Strawberry keeps it in QSettings).
   - "Disconnect" deletes it locally and links to last.fm/settings/applications.
3. **Scrobbling.**
   - Send `track.updateNowPlaying` when playback actually starts, without queueing it.
   - Count real playing time, not playhead position. `play_events.listened_ms` can't be reused.
   - A play qualifies if the track is longer than 30 s and was played for at least half its length or 240 s.
   - Timestamp = start time (UTC). Use `chosenByUser=0` for autoplay and recommender tracks.
   - Queue in a new SQLite table and send oldest first, 50 at a time, over HTTPS POST with `format=json` and User-Agent `Monolist/<version> (+https://github.com/droidboy08-hub/Monolist)`.
   - Always parse the response body:
     - accepted items, and items ignored with codes 1-4: delete.
     - ignored code 5 (daily limit): keep and retry the next UTC day.
     - network errors, HTTP 5xx, 11, 16: exponential backoff.
     - 29: back off for minutes.
     - 9: clear the session, keep the queue, ask the user to reconnect.
     - 10, 13, 26: pause and **keep** the queue.
     - 6 and other per-request errors: drop only the offending item(s).
   - Fix the Settings copy at `SettingsView.qml:416` to say "half of it or four minutes, whichever comes first, for tracks over 30 seconds", and to mention now-playing updates.
   - Consider a small "powered by AudioScrobbler" credit (ToS §2.7).
   - Implement from the spec; Strawberry, Clementine and Tauon are GPL and Cider is AGPL, while Monolist is MIT.

**What the owner must do (only the owner can)**
- (a) Answer ROADMAP.md:193: build Last.fm now or later.
- (b) Sign in to last.fm with the account that should own the app, open https://www.last.fm/api/account/create and enter:
  - Contact email: yours
  - Application name: "Monolist" (users see this on the approval page)
  - Application description: e.g. "Open-source desktop music player (Windows/macOS/Linux) that scrobbles what you play."
  - Callback URL: leave blank (the app passes its own `cb`)
  - Application homepage: https://github.com/droidboy08-hub/Monolist
  - Then submit it yourself.
- (c) Copy the API key and Shared secret from the confirmation page (they stay listed at https://www.last.fm/api/accounts). Keep them in a password manager or as user environment variables or GitHub Actions secrets. **Never** commit them or paste them into issues, chat or logs. Hand them to the macOS build through the same private channel, not the repo.
- (d) Read https://www.last.fm/api/tos and accept it as the key holder: non-commercial only, the attribution clause, and the §5.1 content clause as it relates to yt-dlp streaming, which is your own risk call.
- (e) If you later change your mind and commit the values, expect forks to reuse them, and be ready to rotate the key by creating a new API account.
openQuestions: Build Last.fm now, later, or hide the 'Designed, not built' Connections section? (ROADMAP.md:193)
Which Last.fm account should own the API account: the owner's personal account or a dedicated project account? (The key holder bears ToS responsibility and suspension risk.)

Where will official release builds be produced: on the owner's machines or in GitHub Actions? That decides where the key and secret are kept (local environment variables vs Actions secrets) and how the macOS session gets them.

Will Monolist also use Last.fm read APIs (artist.getInfo, similar artists for artist pages or the recommender)? With one key shared by all users that raises rate-limit (error 29) exposure much more than scrobbling alone.

Store the session key in Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain (shared infrastructure with the planned YouTube cookie sign-in) or in the plain `settings` SQLite table, as Strawberry does with QSettings?
Does Last.fm accept `cb=http://127.0.0.1:<port>/` (the RFC 8252 preference), or should Monolist use `http://localhost:<port>/` as Strawberry does? This can only be tested once an API key exists.

Is the owner comfortable with ToS §5.1's 'illegal or unauthorised use or sharing of content' clause given the yt-dlp/InnerTube streaming? It is worded for websites, and Pear Desktop and Web Scrobbler scrobble YouTube Music openly, but it is still uncertain.
Show the ToS §2.7 'powered by AudioScrobbler' credit (e.g. in Settings > Connections or About)? Most open-source players don't appear to, but the ToS asks for it.

Unverified details: the exact create-form fields (the page needs a login), the 2,800/day and 14-day limits (community-documented only), Navidrome's stated reason for dropping its shared key (Reddit link not reachable), and the Kodi suspension details (forum returned 403).

research.findings:
## Summary

- **Chrome, Edge or Brave cookies on Windows cannot be read by yt-dlp any more.** The Firefox profile route still works in principle.
- **A cookies.txt file from a private window works.** It is manual, though, and the file goes stale in days to weeks.
- **OAuth is not an option.** yt-dlp removed it in November 2024. ytmusicapi's version needs each user to create their own Google Cloud client, and a client registered for the app would break Google's YouTube API policies.
- **The strongest design is a dedicated sign-in web view that the app hosts itself:** WebView2 on Windows and WKWebView on macOS. The web view owns a separate Google session, and the app reads that session's cookies through the native cookie APIs. It carries two risks that are not settled. Google may refuse sign-in inside an embedded WebView2. Device Bound Session Credentials (DBSC, Google's 2026 feature that ties session cookies to one device) may shorten how long lifted cookies keep working.
- **Qt's own web modules cannot do this on the MinGW kit.** Qt WebEngine does not build with MinGW, and Qt WebView's WebView2 plugin only builds with MSVC. Even the MSVC build of Qt WebView never exposes cookie values.

---

## What Monolist does today (read from the code)

- **Three InnerTube clients.** `Client { Music, YouTube, Player }` (`Monolist Player/src/innertube.h:79-87`).
  - Music is `WEB_REMIX`, YouTube is `WEB`, and Player is `VISIONOS` 1.02 with an Apple Vision device profile (`src/innertube.cpp:97-119`).
- **Headers sent on every request.** `InnerTube::post()` sets Content-Type, User-Agent, Origin and Referer (`innertube.cpp:436-445`).
  - Only the Player client adds `X-Goog-Visitor-Id` and a `visitorData` in its context (`innertube.cpp:429-443`).
  - There is no Cookie, Authorization, `X-Goog-AuthUser` or `X-Origin` anywhere in `src/`. A grep for cookie, SAPISID and authorization found no auth code.
- **Anonymous visitor id.** The visitor id is scraped from www.youtube.com (`innertube.cpp:369-405`). `/player` treats `LOGIN_REQUIRED` as "fall through to yt-dlp" (`innertube.cpp:523-529`).
- **yt-dlp gets no cookie options.** It is started with `--ignore-config`, `--js-runtimes deno:…` and similar flags only (`src/ytdlp.cpp:363-379`).
- **Qt modules.** The build links Core, Gui, Quick, QuickControls2, Sql, Svg and Network, and no WebView (`CMakeLists.txt:19`). The local kit `C:\dev\monolist-deps\Qt\6.11.2\mingw_64\plugins` has no `webview` plugin folder.
- **Current Settings design.** The Connections section is design only (`views/SettingsView.qml:393-431`, `components/ServiceRow.qml:5-11,125-134`). Its YouTube Music flow is: export cookies from a private window, give Monolist the file, and keep it "in this computer's keychain".
- **Current roadmap wording.** `ROADMAP.md:193` says "Windows Credential Manager". That store caps a credential blob at 2,560 bytes (see Storage below).
- **Secret files.** No Secrets.plist, .env, cookie or token files were found in Monolist itself. Globbing found Info.plist and entitlement plists only under the old Melody tree and `node_modules`. None were opened.

---

## 1. Cookies from the user's browser (`yt-dlp --cookies-from-browser`)

**Chrome, Edge and Brave on Windows: broken.**
- Chrome 127 (July 2024) introduced app-bound ("v20") encryption on Windows. It ties the cookie key to Chrome's own process ([Google Security Blog, 30 Jul 2024](https://security.googleblog.com/2024/07/improving-security-of-chrome-cookies-on.html), [The Register](https://www.theregister.com/2024/07/31/chrome_appbound_encryption/)).
- yt-dlp's master `cookies.py` only decrypts `v10` on Windows. Every other prefix goes through plain DPAPI, and there is no v20 support at all ([cookies.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/cookies.py)).
- The failure was still being reported on 16 Sep 2026 as "Failed to decrypt with DPAPI" ([yt-music-cli #49](https://github.com/MaheshBhushan/yt-music-cli/issues/49)). The same failure is tracked in the long-open yt-dlp issue ([#10927](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10927)).
- The DevTools-port workaround is also gone. Since Chrome 136, `--remote-debugging-port` is ignored on the default profile, and Google says it did this because attackers used remote debugging to steal cookies after app-bound encryption ([Chrome blog](https://developer.chrome.com/blog/remote-debugging-port)).
- A March 2026 write-up tried DPAPI, rookiepy, DevTools, OAuth and a Data API bearer token. Only Firefox worked ([dev.to, 2 Mar 2026](https://dev.to/osovsky/6-ways-to-get-youtube-cookies-for-yt-dlp-in-2026-only-1-works-2cnb)).
- Edge and Brave use v20 too. Opera, Opera GX and Vivaldi reportedly still use DPAPI v10 ([HackBrowserData](https://hackbrowserdata.org/browsers/)). This is a third-party claim and I did not verify it.

**Firefox: works in principle.**
- Firefox cookies sit in an unencrypted SQLite file, and the yt-dlp FAQ says the method "reportedly works best with Firefox" ([FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ)).
- On Windows the copy of `cookies.sqlite` can still fail with "[Errno 13] Permission denied". That issue was opened 30 Jan 2026 and is still open ([#15760](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15760)).

**macOS.**
- Safari's `Cookies.binarycookies` needs Full Disk Access for the reading process ([#7392](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/7392)).
- App-bound encryption is Windows-only (Google blog above). Chrome on macOS still uses its Keychain-held key, so it is not blocked the same way. I did not re-test this for 2026.

**Structural problem.**
- The cookies belong to a session the browser keeps using and rotating. yt-dlp's own warning is: "The provided YouTube account cookies are no longer valid. They have likely been rotated in the browser as a security measure" ([_base.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_base.py)).
- Re-reading on every run avoids the staleness, but the app and the browser then share one session.

## 2. A cookies.txt file the user exports

**Still works, and it is the method yt-dlp's wiki officially describes** ([Extractors wiki](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors)):
1. Open a private window and sign in.
2. In that same tab, go to `https://www.youtube.com/robots.txt`.
3. Export the youtube.com cookies.
4. Close the window, so the session is never used in a browser again.

The wiki warns not to use `--cookies-from-browser` for this, because that exports the normal profile.
- **Format.** The file must be Netscape format, starting with `# Netscape HTTP Cookie File`. A 400 error is a sign of wrong newlines ([FAQ](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/FAQ)).
- **Chrome still works this way.** An extension reads cookies through the browser's own API, so app-bound encryption does not matter ([gytmdl README](https://github.com/glomatico/gytmdl) points to Firefox and Chromium exporter extensions).
- **Extension risk.** The dev.to author warns against third-party cookie-export extensions because some have carried malware.
- **Lifetime.** Reports range from "3-5 days, even in incognito" ([#13964, Aug 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/13964)) to "days to a few weeks" ([Tunelio, 7 Sep 2026](https://tunelio.dev/blog/yt-dlp-cookies/)) and "~2 weeks" (dev.to 2026).
- **Friction.** It is manual, and it has to be repeated.

## 3. Embedded sign-in web view

**Qt WebEngine is out on MinGW.** "Currently, Qt WebEngine does not compile with MinGW" ([Qt 6.11.2 platform notes](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwebengine-platform-notes.html)).

**Qt WebView's WebView2 backend is MSVC-only.**
- Qt 6.10 added a WebView2 plugin ([Qt 6.10 blog](https://www.qt.io/blog/qt-6.10-released)), and the 6.11 docs say Windows can use Qt WebEngine or WebView2 ([Qt WebView](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwebview-index.html)).
- The plugin's build condition in the 6.11 branch is `CONDITION WIN32 AND MSVC AND WebView2_FOUND` ([configure.cmake](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt/qtwebview/6.11/src/webview/configure.cmake)).
- So the MinGW kit has neither backend on Windows.

**Even with MSVC, Qt WebView does not expose cookie values.**
- The QML `WebView` has `cookieAdded(domain, name)` and `setCookie`/`deleteCookie` only ([QML WebView](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qml-qtwebview-webview.html)).
- The Qt 6.11 C++ `QWebView` (a QWindow, technology preview, [Qt blog 4 May 2026](https://www.qt.io/blog/using-the-webview-module-with-c-and-qt-widgets)) lists only `deleteAllCookies()` among cookie functions ([QWebView](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qwebview.html)).
- The WebView2 plugin's source emits only the domain and name. Its profile lives in `AppLocalDataLocation/WebView2` ([qwebview2webview.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qt/qtwebview/dev/src/plugins/windows/qwebview2webview.cpp)).
- The only Qt-only route would be running the InnerTube calls inside the page with `runJavaScript`. That is MSVC-only on Windows.

**Hosting WebView2 directly under MinGW is feasible.**
- webview/webview (MIT, [LICENSE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/webview/webview/master/LICENSE)) lists LLVM MinGW, MSYS2 and WinLibs as known to work.
- It needs `WebView2.h` from the SDK. It uses either the official `WebView2Loader.dll` or its own minimal built-in loader ([README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/webview/webview/master/README.md), [PR #783](https://github.com/webview/webview/pull/783)).
- MinGW can only link the loader dynamically. The WRL helper headers are MSVC-centric: MSYS2's webview2-loader package breaks on `wrl/implements.h` ([msys2 #30940](https://github.com/msys2/MINGW-packages/issues/30940)). So the COM handler classes have to be written by hand, as webview/webview does.
- `webview_get_native_handle(…BROWSER_CONTROLLER)` returns an `ICoreWebView2Controller*` on Windows, a `WKWebView*` on macOS and a `WebKitWebView*` on GTK ([types.h](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/webview/webview/master/core/include/webview/types.h)). That makes it a single path for all three desktops.
- Before Windows 11, the WebView2 Runtime has to be installed (README).

**Reading cookies back works on both platforms.**
- WebView2: `ICoreWebView2CookieManager::GetCookies` returns every cookie in the profile when the URI is empty (SDK 1.0.705.50+). Each `ICoreWebView2Cookie` exposes `get_Value` and `get_IsHttpOnly`, so HttpOnly cookies are included ([CookieManager](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/reference/win32/icorewebview2cookiemanager), [Cookie](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/reference/win32/icorewebview2cookie)).
- macOS: `WKHTTPCookieStore` getAllCookies plus an observer ([Apple](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/webkit/wkhttpcookiestore)).
- Kaset, a native macOS YouTube Music app, does exactly this in 2026 ([architecture.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sozercan/kaset/main/docs/architecture.md)):
  - a WKWebView login sheet
  - a persistent `WKWebsiteDataStore`
  - a `WKHTTPCookieStoreObserver`
  - "`.loggedIn` | Valid `__Secure-3PAPISID` cookie found"
  - SAPISIDHASH computed natively
  - auth cookies backed up to the Keychain

**Google's embedded-browser block is the big risk.**
- Google blocked Google sign-in from embedded frameworks such as CEF from Jan 2021 ([Google Developers Blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/guidance-to-developers-affected-by-our-effort-to-block-less-secure-browsers-and-applications/)). OAuth in webviews gets `disallowed_useragent` ([Google Developers Blog](https://developers.googleblog.com/upcoming-security-changes-to-googles-oauth-20-authorization-endpoint-in-embedded-webviews/)).
- Microsoft's 2021 position was that Google auth flows "will not be supported in WebView2". Later user reports are mixed: one in May 2023 says Google login worked ([WebView2Feedback #3828](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/discussions/3828)), while others show "This browser or app may not be secure" ([#2552](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/2552)).
- One macOS app notes: "Google rejects embedded web views at sign-in, so both web views report a genuine Safari user agent" ([music-for-youtube](https://github.com/emonsaqibh/music-for-youtube)).
- **Uncertain for WebView2 in 2026.** It needs a hands-on spike before anything is committed to.

## 4. OAuth

**yt-dlp.**
- Official OAuth using the YouTube-on-TV device-code client arrived in 2024.10.22 ([coletdjnz plugin README](https://github.com/coletdjnz/yt-dlp-youtube-oauth2)).
- It was reverted in "[ie/youtube] Remove broken OAuth support (#11558)", merged 16 Nov 2024 ([PR](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/pull/11558), [commit](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/commit/52c0ffe40ad6e8404d93296f575007b05b04c686)). The trigger was OAuth requests failing with HTTP 400 "invalid argument" while cookies still worked ([#11462](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11462)).
- The wiki's only explanation: "Due to new restrictions enacted by YouTube, logging in with OAuth no longer works with yt-dlp." The current `_base.py` says "Login with OAuth is no longer supported." The exact server-side mechanism was never documented, so this is uncertain.
- Separately, some accounts get only DRM formats on the TV client ([#12563](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12563)).
- Reusing Google's YouTube-TV client ID from a third-party app also means impersonating Google's own app.

**The app's own OAuth client.**
- Google's device flow does allow the `youtube` and `youtube.readonly` scopes, and it assumes the app cannot keep its client secret secret ([Google](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2/limited-input-device)).
- YouTube scopes are sensitive. An unverified project gets a lifetime cap of 100 new users and an "unverified app" warning ([Google Cloud help](https://support.google.com/cloud/answer/7454865)).
- Verification binds the developer to the [YouTube API Services Developer Policies](https://developers.google.com/youtube/terms/developer-policies). Those forbid reverse-engineering undocumented YouTube API services, separating audio from video, scraping and background players. The listed penalties include "termination of the Google account" behind the client.
- For a public MIT repo that uses InnerTube, this route is not viable.

## 5. ytmusicapi (1.12.x, 2026)

**Browser authentication.**
- The user pastes the request headers of an authenticated POST to music.youtube.com: Cookie, Authorization, X-Goog-AuthUser and x-origin.
- The docs say the credentials "remain valid as long as your YTMusic browser session is valid (about 2 years unless you log out)" ([browser.html](https://ytmusicapi.readthedocs.io/en/stable/setup/browser.html)). That claim is dated and conflicts with the 2025-26 yt-dlp reports above.
- It recomputes the Authorization header on every request from `__Secure-3PAPISID` and the origin ([helpers.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigma67/ytmusicapi/main/ytmusicapi/helpers.py), [ytmusic.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigma67/ytmusicapi/main/ytmusicapi/ytmusic.py)).
- Brand accounts are handled with `context.user.onBehalfOfUser` (ytmusic.py).

**OAuth.**
- "As of November 2024" users must bring their own client ID and secret of the "TVs and Limited Input devices" type ([oauth.html](https://ytmusicapi.readthedocs.io/en/latest/setup/oauth.html)).
- Google disabled OAuth "for the web client" in Nov 2024, and the maintainer recommends browser auth ([#679](https://github.com/sigma67/ytmusicapi/issues/679), [discussion #682](https://github.com/sigma67/ytmusicapi/discussions/682)).
- OAuth broke again in 1.12.0 (May 2026). It was fixed via PR #932 ([#921](https://github.com/sigma67/ytmusicapi/issues/921), [1.12.2 release](https://github.com/sigma67/ytmusicapi/releases/tag/1.12.2)).
- Uploads need browser auth: "OAuth credentials do not work for uploads" ([setup](https://ytmusicapi.readthedocs.io/en/stable/setup/index.html)).

**What needs auth.** Every library method calls `_check_auth()` ([library reference](https://ytmusicapi.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference/library.html), [library.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sigma67/ytmusicapi/main/ytmusicapi/mixins/library.py)):

| Area | Endpoint |
|---|---|
| Library playlists | `FEmusic_liked_playlists` |
| Library songs | `FEmusic_liked_videos` |
| Library albums | `FEmusic_liked_albums` |
| Library artists / subscriptions | `FEmusic_library_corpus_track_artists`, `FEmusic_library_corpus_artists` |
| History | `FEmusic_history` |
| Add to history | the `videostatsPlaybackUrl` from `playbackTracking` |
| Ratings | `like/like`, `like/dislike` |
| Library edits | `feedback` |
| Subscriptions | `subscription/subscribe` |
| Account | `account/account_menu` |

## How authenticated InnerTube requests are made

From yt-dlp's current `_base.py` ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_base.py)):

- **Cookies used.** The SID cookie is `SAPISID` or `__Secure-3PAPISID`. `__Secure-1PAPISID` and `__Secure-3PAPISID` feed the other two schemes.
- **Header format.** Each scheme is `f'{scheme} {ts}_{sha1(" ".join([user_session_id?, ts, sid, origin]))}[_u]'`. The three schemes `SAPISIDHASH`, `SAPISID1PHASH` and `SAPISID3PHASH` are space-joined into one `Authorization` header. The `_u` suffix and prefix appear only when a user session id is known.
- **Other headers.** `X-Origin` is set to the same origin whenever Authorization is sent. `X-Goog-AuthUser` is the session index, 0 by default. Delegated (brand) accounts add `X-Goog-PageId`. `X-Youtube-Bootstrap-Logged-In: true` is sent when LOGGED_IN. `X-Goog-Visitor-Id` is still sent.
- **Signed-in test.** yt-dlp treats a session as signed in when `LOGIN_INFO` plus one of the SAPISID cookies is present.
- **For Monolist.** The origin to hash is `https://music.youtube.com` for `Client::Music` (`innertube.cpp:422-424` already sends that Origin).

## Cookie rotation and session lifetime

- **Rotation in browsers.** Browsers rotate `__Secure-1PSIDTS`, `__Secure-3PSIDTS`, `SIDCC` and `__Secure-1PSIDCC`. On other Google properties, an open browser calls `POST https://accounts.google.com/RotateCookies`, whose reply declares a 600 s interval.
- **Evidence from a Google tool (NotebookLM).** A session with no rotation "died at T+20m" while a rotated one lived past 2 h ([notebooklm-py #345, May 2026](https://github.com/teng-lin/notebooklm-py/issues/345)). This is evidence from NotebookLM and not verified for YouTube, where frozen private-window exports last days to weeks.
- **DBSC (new in 2026).**
  - Device Bound Session Credentials went GA in Chrome 146 on Windows. The rollout started 25 May 2026 and covers personal Google accounts too, with no user or admin off switch ([Workspace Updates](https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2026/05/prevent-account-takeovers-with-DBSC-now-generally-available-in-the-Chrome-browser-for-Windows.html), [The Hacker News](https://thehackernews.com/2026/04/google-rolls-out-dbsc-in-chrome-146-to.html)).
  - macOS support is planned.
  - Edge 147 (Apr 2026) also lists DBSC, and WebView2 Runtime 147 is on the same engine ([Edge 147 notes](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/web-platform/release-notes/147)).
  - As of May 2026, RotateCookies still worked for bound sessions. Google "may eventually enforce `RotateBoundCookies`" (notebooklm-py #345).
  - **Consequence:** cookies lifted out of a browser or web view may stop being refreshable anywhere except inside the web view that holds the device key. The web view should therefore stay the owner of the session.

## What sign-in unlocks

- **Account data.** Library, liked songs (`LM`), own and private playlists, history, subscribed artists, podcasts and channels, ratings, and uploads (browser auth only). All require auth, per the ytmusicapi docs above.
- **Personalised home.** Requesting `FEmusic_home` with cookies returns the account's feed. This is inferred: ytmusicapi does not state it explicitly.
- **Premium streams.** itag 141 (AAC 256 kbps) and 774 (Opus 256 kbps) need cookies and an active Premium subscription ([gytmdl](https://github.com/glomatico/gytmdl)); some users could not get them even with cookies ([#12891, Apr 2025](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/12891)).
  - yt-dlp's `_DEFAULT_PREMIUM_CLIENTS = ('web_creator', 'tv_downgraded', 'web')`, with the comment "Premium does not require POT" ([_video.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_video.py)).
  - The PO Token guide: "GVS PO Token is not required for YouTube Premium subscribers" ([PO Token Guide](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/PO-Token-Guide)).
- **Rate limits and bot checks.** The yt-dlp wiki gives roughly 300 videos per hour as a guest against roughly 2,000 per hour signed in (Extractors wiki), so fewer bot checks.
- **Cost to playback.**
  - yt-dlp's `visionos` client has no `SUPPORTS_COOKIES` (the default is False). Monolist's fast tier (`innertube.cpp:106-119`) therefore cannot carry the account and should stay anonymous.
  - Passing cookies switches yt-dlp to `_DEFAULT_AUTHED_CLIENTS = ('web_embedded', 'tv_downgraded', 'web')` (_video.py). Web clients then need a GVS PO token or get SABR-only formats (PO Token Guide).
  - One 2026 report: with cookies, only 7 formats appeared against 28 without ([#16229, Mar 2026](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/16229)).

## Account risks

- **yt-dlp's warning.** "By using your account with yt-dlp, you run the risk of it being banned (temporarily or permanently)" (Extractors wiki).
- **Account-level blocking.** Accounts have been blocked on web clients with "This content isn't available" while the Android app still worked ([#10085, Jun 2024](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10085)).
- **No answer on scope.** A January 2026 question about whether a ban reaches Gmail or Drive has no maintainer reply ([#15724](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/15724)).
- **YouTube Terms of Service** (effective 15 Dec 2023, [ToS](https://www.youtube.com/t/terms)) forbid:
  - downloading except as authorised
  - circumventing security features
  - access "using any automated means"
- **Current UI copy.** The "account you can afford to lose" caution in `SettingsView.qml:424` matches this evidence.

## Storage

- **Windows Credential Manager is too small.** `CredWrite` blobs are capped at `CRED_MAX_CREDENTIAL_BLOB_SIZE` = 5×512 = 2,560 bytes ([CREDENTIALW](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincred/ns-wincred-credentialw)). A full signed-in youtube.com cookie set may well be larger; I have not measured it.
- **Better options.** QtKeychain can fall back to `CryptProtectData`, i.e. DPAPI ([qtkeychain](https://github.com/frankosterfeld/qtkeychain/)), or the app can write a DPAPI-encrypted file itself. The macOS Keychain has no such limit (Kaset uses it).
- **The web-view profile is itself a credential store.** On sign-out it must be cleared with `DeleteAllCookies` and its folder deleted.

**Build the sign-in as a dedicated embedded web view that owns its own Google session. Keep a cookies.txt import as the fallback that always works, and add Firefox auto-import only as a convenience.**

**1. Spike first.** It takes about half a day and is the step that decides whether the web view approach works. Build a tiny MinGW test program that uses webview/webview (MIT). It supports MinGW, can use `WebView2Loader.dll` or its own loader, and exposes `ICoreWebView2Controller*` / `WKWebView*` / `WebKitWebView*` through `webview_get_native_handle`. The test should:
- open `accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?continue=https://music.youtube.com` in a WebView2 with its own user-data folder;
- ask the user to sign in by hand;
- read the cookies back with `ICoreWebView2CookieManager::GetCookies("")`.

Also check whether Google shows "This browser or app may not be secure", and whether overriding the user agent to plain Edge changes that. On macOS, the other session can use WKWebView with a Safari user agent, which Kaset and music-for-youtube show working in 2026.

**2. If the spike works, the architecture is:**
- The sign-in window is a native top-level window. It holds WebView2 on Windows through hand-written COM (no WRL), WKWebView on macOS in Objective-C++, and later WebKitGTK on Linux, all through the same webview/webview seam.
  - Don't use Qt WebView here: under MinGW it has no Windows backend (`CONDITION WIN32 AND MSVC`), and it never exposes cookie values.
- The web view's persistent profile is the source of truth. At app start, and every few hours, silently load `https://music.youtube.com` in a hidden web view so Google rotates the session inside the engine that holds any DBSC device key. Then re-read all cookies, including HttpOnly ones, into a dedicated `QNetworkCookieJar`.
- Only `Client::Music` (and optionally `Client::YouTube`) requests carry the account. They send the Cookie header, `Authorization` built from the SAPISIDHASH, SAPISID1PHASH and SAPISID3PHASH schemes over `https://music.youtube.com`, plus `X-Origin` and `X-Goog-AuthUser: 0`. Brand accounts need `onBehalfOfUser` or `X-Goog-PageId`.
- Detect a dead session through `account/account_menu`, or by the absence of logged-in markers, and prompt the user to sign in again.
- Keep the VISIONOS `/player` tier and yt-dlp anonymous by default. The account then only ever makes library-style requests, which lowers the ban risk. It also avoids the PO-token and SABR fallout of yt-dlp's authenticated clients.
- Offer an explicit opt-in: "Use my Premium for 256 kbps". It writes a temporary Netscape cookies file for yt-dlp's premium clients (`web_creator`, `tv_downgraded`, `web`) and deletes it after the run.
- Store any exported cookie copy with DPAPI on Windows and in the Keychain on macOS, not in Windows Credential Manager (2,560-byte cap). Update `ROADMAP.md:193` and the Settings steps at `SettingsView.qml:426-429` to match. On sign-out, call `DeleteAllCookies`, delete the profile folder and delete the stored copy.

**3. If Google blocks WebView2 sign-in,** ship the design that already exists:
- a cookies.txt import from a private window, following yt-dlp's robots.txt procedure;
- plus a "Read from Firefox" button that opens `cookies.sqlite` read-only.

**Do not build:**
- Chrome, Edge or Brave extraction (v20 app-bound encryption, still failing in September 2026);
- any OAuth route: the TV client was removed from yt-dlp, and the app's own Google client would fall under the YouTube API Developer Policies with a 100-user cap.

- **The URL** is `https://accounts.google.com/ServiceLogin?service=youtube&continue=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2F` (GoogleAccountSheet.swift:77-92).

Landing on music minted a separate "YouTube Music session" (its own SID/SAPISID, visitorData, LOGIN_INFO and a large YNID). Playback then presented that session on a WEB `/player` call, and the identities did not match (GoogleAccountSheet.swift:78-89).
  - Opening music.youtube.com directly does not work as a sign-in entry point, because YTM happily renders signed out (GoogleAccountSheet.swift:17-21).

The comment says Google refuses credentials from a UA it recognises as an embedded web view ("this browser or app may not be secure").
- **Sign-in detection** is in `didFinish`, once the host contains `youtube.com` (GoogleAccountSheet.swift:127-161):
  - It reads the whole cookie store and requires `SAPISID` or `__Secure-3PAPISID`. The comment explains that SID/HSID alone are not enough, and that without SAPISID InnerTube "quietly serves the generic feed with a 200" (130-136).
  - It then runs `SessionBootstrap.ytcfgHarvestJS` on that signed-in page to capture `ID_TOKEN`, `DATASYNC_ID`, `VISITOR_DATA` and related values (139-146).
  - Only after that does it navigate to account settings. Navigating first "left experimental playback with cookies but no idToken" (139-141).
  - If the harvest fails, it falls back to `SessionBootstrap.refresh()` (147-151).
- **`onSessionChanged` fires twice**: once on confirmed sign-in, and again on `onDisappear`. Google's account page has its own sign-out button, which drops the cookies while the persisted flag still says signed in (GoogleAccountSheet.swift:24-33, 59-62).

## 2. How cookies and tokens are captured
- **Cookies.** Every consumer reads `WKWebsiteDataStore.default().httpCookieStore.getAllCookies`. That one store is shared by the login sheet and the hidden bootstrap web view (GoogleAccountSheet.swift:66-69; YouTubeAuth.swift:151-154; YouTubeAccountSync.swift:1115-1120; YouTubeSession.swift:96-98).
- **ytcfg values.** A hidden, persistent `SessionBootstrap` WKWebView loads `https://www.youtube.com` at launch with a desktop-Safari UA (SessionBootstrap.swift:87-117). The injected JS reads, from `ytcfg.data_` or `ytcfg.get`:
  - `VISITOR_DATA`, `PO_TOKEN`, `DATASYNC_ID`, `ID_TOKEN`
  - `PAGE_CL`, `PAGE_BUILD_LABEL`, the InnerTube client version, `STS`
  - `DEVICE_EXPERIMENT_ID`, `ROLLOUT_TOKEN`, `CLICKTRACKING_PARAMS`
  - the `WEB_PLAYER_CONTEXT_CONFIGS.configInfo` hashes

  (SessionBootstrap.swift:161-188; applied at 276-309). The bootstrap loads signed out and "will not grow" an ID_TOKEN unless it is re-read, so `ensureIdTokenForSignedInPlayback()` reloads it while signed in (SessionBootstrap.swift:54-58, 205-218).
- **PO token.** `PoTokenMinter` runs BotGuard in a hidden 1x1 WKWebView holding a local HTML interpreter page, ported from NewPipe and yt-dlp WebPO (PoTokenMinter.swift:4-23):
  1. `POST /api/jnn/v1/Create`
  2. `runBotGuard` in JS
  3. `POST /api/jnn/v1/GenerateIT` for the integrity token
  4. JS `obtainPoToken(identifier)` to mint the token

  The integrity token is reused for the server's TTL minus 10 minutes, capped at 6 hours (PoTokenMinter.swift:191-194). The token binds to `dataSyncId` when signed in and `visitorData` when a guest (SessionBootstrap.swift:406-419).

## 3. How it is stored
- **Google cookies live only in WebKit's persistent default website data store**, not the Keychain. The comment at GoogleAccountSheet.swift:66-69 relies on this.
- `isYouTubeLoggedIn`, `ytDisplayName` and `ytProfileImageURL` are persisted through `PersistenceStore`, which wraps `UserDefaults.standard` (PlayerState.swift:43-56; PersistenceStore.swift:90-97).
- `visitorData`, `idToken`, `dataSyncId` and the PO token are **in memory only** and re-harvested each launch (SessionBootstrap.swift:42-69).
- The Last.fm API key comes from the bundled `Secrets.plist`, with an Info.plist fallback (LastFmClient.swift:7-33).

## 4. Refresh and revalidation
- **Launch sequence** (musicplayerApp.swift:123-143):
  1. Remove any canned consent cookie.
  2. `SessionBootstrap.start()`.
  3. `waitUntilReady()` (up to 6s).
  4. `revalidateSession`.
- **Foreground** repeats steps 2-4 (musicplayerApp.swift:158-177).
- `revalidateSession` is throttled to one definitive check per 1800s (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:151-159).
- **The check** is an authed `FEmusic_home` call:
  - It accepts only `responseContext.serviceTrackingParams` `logged_in=1`.
  - An absent param falls back to looking for personalised shelf titles or an account name.
  - It is three-state: `active`, `rejected` or `unavailable`. Only 401/403 or `logged_in=0` clears the login (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:97-105, 233-343).
- **An empty cookie read counts as `unavailable`**, retried twice at 400ms. iOS reclaims the web content process in the background and the store can read empty (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:239-252, 1096-1113).
- **Cookie rotation is never explicitly handled.** All API requests set `httpShouldHandleCookies = false` (YouTubeAuth.swift:93; YouTubeAccountSync.swift:1162; YouTubeResolver.swift:205), so `Set-Cookie` headers on API responses are never written back. Rotation of `__Secure-*PSIDTS` and `SIDCC` is presumably absorbed by the hidden web view reloading www.youtube.com into the same store. That is my inference; no code comment says so.
- **Sign-out** deletes 15 named auth cookies and leaves the visitor cookies alone (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:161-190).
- `YouTubeAuth.invalidate()` must run on sign-in and sign-out. The cached value used to outlive login (YouTubeAuth.swift:135-140).

## 5. How authenticated requests are built: three separate formatters that disagree
**A. Explore / account (`YouTubeAccountSync.makeRequest`, YouTubeAccountSync.swift:1156-1183)**
- Cookies are scoped to what a browser would send to `music.youtube.com`, deduplicated by name with the most specific domain winning (1123-1143).
- Headers: `Origin`, `X-Origin` and `Referer` set to `https://music.youtube.com`; a desktop Chrome UA; `X-YouTube-Client-Name: 67`; `X-YouTube-Client-Version: 1.20250519.03.01`; `X-Goog-AuthUser: 0`.
- `Authorization` carries space-separated `SAPISIDHASH`, `SAPISID1PHASH` and `SAPISID3PHASH` values. Each is `ts_` + lowercase SHA-1 of `"<ts> <cookie> <origin>"`, and each label is paired with **its own** cookie (1065-1089).
- The body context is `WEB_REMIX`.

**B. Signed-in playback (`YouTubeAuth` plus `YouTubeResolver`)**
- A single `SAPISIDHASH ts_HEX_u`: **uppercase** hex, with the hash input `"<userSessionId> <ts> <SAPISID> <origin>"`. The user session id is parsed from `DATASYNC_ID` split on `||` (YouTubeAuth.swift:44-88).
- Cookies are scoped to `www.youtube.com` and filtered to a 21-name allow-list. That drops `_gcl_au`, `CONSISTENCY` and `LOGIN_INFO` because "extra is its own signature" (YouTubeAuth.swift:171-198).
- `idToken` goes into `context.client` (YouTubeAuth.swift:118-122).
- The `/player` POST goes to `www.youtube.com/youtubei/v1/player` (YouTubeResolver.swift:162-245). It uses client `WEB` 1.20250602.08.00 with a Safari UA (the yt-dlp `web_safari` recipe), the `X-YouTube-Page-CL` / `Page-Label` values, `X-Goog-Visitor-Id`, `X-Origin`, `Cookie` and `Authorization`.
- The **same auth headers go on every HLS manifest and segment GET** (MusicPlayer.swift:1014-1048).
- For comparison, yt-dlp's `_make_sid_authorization` also prefixes the user session id (from `DATASYNC_ID`) as the `u` part and emits all three hash schemes. Its hex is lowercase via `hexdigest()` ([yt-dlp _base.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/yt_dlp/extractor/youtube/_base.py)).

**C. Classic engine (`YouTubeSession.build`)**
- It joins **every** youtube.com and google.com cookie **unscoped** and appends a canned SOCS (YouTubeSession.swift:100-109).
- It hashes `__Secure-3PAPISID` first but labels the result `SAPISIDHASH`, in lowercase and without `_u` (YouTubeSession.swift:110-111, 134-142).
- Section A's own comments describe both of those as silently breaking auth (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:1067-1072, 1123-1129). YouTubeAuth.swift:11-14 says keeping B and C separate is intentional.

## 6. Features that used the signed-in session
The account scope is **read-only by design**: "No library sync, no importing YTM playlists/likes, no write-backs" (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:11-14; AccountView.swift:99-101).
- **Personalised Explore home.** `FEmusic_home` with continuations (up to 8 shelves) plus mood chips (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:226-318). It feeds YouTubeShelfProvider.swift:148 and RecommendationEngine.swift:1089.
- **Account name and avatar** from `account/account_menu` (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:72-93).
- **Authed-if-possible browse:**
  - playlist and album tracks, and see-all pages (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:450-474, 557-603)
  - `/next` related tracks (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:688-745)
- **Signed-in playback lane.** WEB `/player` returns `hlsManifestUrl`, which plays through `HLSProxyLoader` (YouTubeResolver.swift:3-14, 67-158; MusicPlayer.swift:760-793). It is used for High quality, when the network has bot-walled both anonymous lanes, or when Settings > Support "Signed-in lane only" is on (MusicPlayer.swift:642-676; SettingsState.swift:183-187).
- **Classic-engine calls that carry the whole jar:**
  - metadata backfill (PlayerState.swift:682, 788, 1003)
  - PlaylistImporter (PlaylistImporter.swift:112-129)
- Signing in is labelled "(Optional)" and "only personalises what Explore serves" (SettingsView.swift:346-352; AccountView.swift:102-106).

## 7. Problems the comments and diagnostics record
- **Embedded-UA block** ("this browser or app may not be secure"), worked around with a UA spoof (GoogleAccountSheet.swift:94-98).
- **Silent auth failure.** Bad auth returns HTTP 200 with a generic feed, so only `logged_in=1` can be trusted (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:22-26, 320-329).
  - `AuthDiagnostics` exists to test this: it fires `FEmusic_home` under five header/cookie variants and reports which one returns `logged_in=1`. It prints cookie names only, never values (AuthDiagnostics.swift:5-23, 39-53). It is run with the `AUTH_TEST` launch argument (musicplayerApp.swift:18-23).
- **Cookie handling mistakes that broke auth:**
  - Duplicate cookie names across `.google.com` and `youtube.com` produced `logged_in=0` (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:1123-1129).
  - A hash label paired with the wrong cookie was rejected (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:1067-1072).
  - The `_u` suffix without the session id got 200 but no HLS (YouTubeAuth.swift:44-50).
- **Missing idToken.** Anonymous WEB `/player` returns `LOGIN_REQUIRED`; with cookies, the hash and idToken it returns streamingData (YouTubeAuth.swift:7-9). The idToken went missing when the harvest ran too late (GoogleAccountSheet.swift:139-141).
- **Bot checks and PO tokens:**
  - "Sign in to confirm you're not a bot" appeared on every client while signed in, because the PO token was bound to the guest visitorData instead of dataSyncId (SessionBootstrap.swift:406-415; PoTokenMinter.swift:130-135).
  - Anonymous VISIONOS, IOS, ANDROID and ANDROID_VR were all bot-walled at the tester's site. A 15-minute `AnonymousLaneGate` now skips them there (PlaybackChain.swift:27-80).
  - An ANDROID request carrying a WEB-minted PO token was one more reason to be refused (InnerTubeAPI.swift:381-400).
  - A PO token on googlevideo URLs caused 403s on segments (MusicPlayer.swift:948-953; YouTubeResolver.swift:130-133).
  - `serviceIntegrityDimensions` turned plain stream URLs into ciphered ones, so it is withheld (YouTubeResolver.swift:190-195).
  - Waiting on BotGuard cost about 4s per launch, so the app no longer waits (SessionBootstrap.swift:438-454).
- **The session appeared to sign itself out.** Causes found: a launch race on a cold cookie store (musicplayerApp.swift:131-142); a network hiccup treated as a logout (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:97-105); and an empty store after iOS reclaimed the process (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:239-251).
- **Consent cookie.** A canned SOCS written into the store broke the bootstrap (no VISITOR_DATA). It is now header-only and removed at launch (YouTubeConsentCookie.swift:24-43, 57-79; musicplayerApp.swift:126-129).
- **Stale comments.** Several comments still say "music.youtube.com" after the move to www: SessionBootstrap.swift:158-160 and 190, and the log line at GoogleAccountSheet.swift:154. YouTubeAccountSync.swift:16-20 says authed calls carry nothing from the bootstrap, but `postNext` attaches the bootstrap visitorData to authed requests (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:691, 713-726).

## 8. Last.fm
- **`LastFmClient` is metadata only**, using `ws.audioscrobbler.com/2.0/` with an api_key (LastFmClient.swift:3-46). It implements:
  - `track.search`, used for supplementary search results (LastFmClient.swift:48-56; SearchView.swift:719)
  - `chart.gettoptracks` and `chart.gettoptags`, used for trending (LastFmClient.swift:58-75; SearchView.swift:779-783)
- **There is no Last.fm auth, session key or scrobbling.** The Settings row is a cosmetic "Coming soon" (SettingsView.swift:237-246, 322-335).

## 9. What ports to Monolist (Qt 6.11, MinGW 13, Windows now; macOS and Linux later)
Monolist today has no cookie or auth code. `src/innertube.cpp` only scrapes `visitorData` from www.youtube.com (`Monolist Player\src\innertube.cpp:369-405`) and sends it as `X-Goog-Visitor-Id` (innertube.cpp:429-443). `ytdlp.cpp` passes no `--cookies` (ytdlp.cpp:360-387). CMake links only Core, Gui, Quick, QuickControls2, Sql, Svg and Network (`Monolist Player\CMakeLists.txt:19`). The Connections rows are design-only (`views\SettingsView.qml:394-432`; `components\ServiceRow.qml:5-11`).

**The iOS embedded-web-view sign-in does not port cleanly to Windows with MinGW:**
- **Qt WebEngine:** "Currently, Qt WebEngine does not compile with MinGW" ([Qt WebEngine platform notes](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwebengine-platform-notes.html)). Using it would mean switching the toolchain to MSVC.
- **Qt WebView:** on Windows it uses WebEngine or WebView2, and on macOS the system web view ([Qt WebView](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwebview-index.html)). Its QML API has `setCookie`, `deleteCookie`, `deleteAllCookies` and `runJavaScript`, but **no way to read cookie values**. `cookieAdded` fires for site-set cookies only on the WebEngine backend ([WebView QML type](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qml-qtwebview-webview.html)).
  - HttpOnly session cookies such as SID/HSID/SSID/__Secure-*PSID could therefore not be captured. That these particular cookies are HttpOnly is from general knowledge; I did not verify it here.
  - The local Qt install `C:\dev\monolist-deps\Qt\6.11.2\mingw_64` has **no Qt WebView module**: no `Qt6Web*` DLLs, no plugins, no `lib\cmake\Qt6WebView`. I checked this read-only.
  - Whether Qt's MinGW builds ship the WebView2 plugin is **unverified**.
- **Native WebView2:** `ICoreWebView2CookieManager::GetCookies` returns every cookie in the profile, including HttpOnly ([MS Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-edge/webview2/reference/win32/icorewebview2cookiemanager?view=webview2-1.0.2420.47)). But using the WebView2 SDK from MinGW is **unverified**, and Google sign-in inside WebView2 is reported to fail with "This browser or app may not be secure" ([WebView2Feedback #1584](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/1584), [#2552](https://github.com/MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback/issues/2552)).
- **Google policy:** sign-in from embedded browser frameworks has been blocked since 4 January 2021, and Google tells developers to use browser-based OAuth instead ([Google Developers Blog, Aug 2020](https://developers.googleblog.com/guidance-to-developers-affected-by-our-effort-to-block-less-secure-browsers-and-applications/)). The iOS UA spoof is a workaround against that policy and could break at any time.
- **OAuth:** YouTube login through OAuth or device code no longer works in yt-dlp; cookies are the only path ([yt-dlp #11462](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11462), [#11585](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/11585)). So there is no supported OAuth route to reuse either.

**The cookie-file route in Monolist's design (SettingsView.qml:427-430) matches yt-dlp's documented method:**
- The wiki's steps: a private window, visit `youtube.com/robots.txt`, export the cookies, then close the window so YouTube does not rotate them. The same page warns the account may be "banned (temporarily or permanently)" and gives about 2000 videos/hour logged in versus about 300 as a guest ([yt-dlp Extractors wiki](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/Extractors)).
- **Watch-out:** yt-dlp's `--cookies FILE` both reads and **"dump[s] cookie jar in"** that file ([yt-dlp README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/master/README.md)). If the jar lives in a keychain, Monolist would need to write a temporary file per run and read rotations back.
- `--cookies-from-browser chrome` on Windows is unreliable because of Chrome 127+ App-Bound encryption ([yt-dlp #10927](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/issues/10927)).

**Logic that ports directly into C++ `QNetworkAccessManager` code, independent of the browser:**
1. Scope the cookie jar per host, deduplicate names with the most specific domain winning, and filter to a browser-like allow-list (YouTubeAuth.swift:156-198; YouTubeAccountSync.swift:1130-1143).
2. Build SAPISIDHASH the way yt-dlp does: the `u` prefix from `DATASYNC_ID`, all three schemes each paired with its own cookie, SHA-1 via `QCryptographicHash`. The iOS code is inconsistent about uppercase versus lowercase hex; yt-dlp uses lowercase.
3. Send `X-Goog-AuthUser: 0` and `X-Origin`.
4. Harvest `DATASYNC_ID`, `ID_TOKEN` and visitorData by fetching www.youtube.com **with the cookies**. The existing regex scrape at innertube.cpp:371-397 can be extended for this.
5. Validate with `logged_in=1` using the three-state rule: never sign out on a network failure (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:97-105, 320-343).
6. Use the signed-in `web_safari` WEB `/player` call to get HLS, with the auth headers on segment GETs as well. yt-dlp's guide says web_safari's HLS formats do not require a GVS PO token "at this time" (page updated 12 July 2026) ([PO Token Guide](https://github.com/yt-dlp/yt-dlp/wiki/PO-Token-Guide)). That agrees with the iOS finding that sending a PO token was harmful (MusicPlayer.swift:948-953).
7. Surgical sign-out that deletes only the auth cookies (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:166-172).
8. Keep the account read-only, as iOS did.

**Storage:** the Monolist copy promises "kept in this computer's keychain" (SettingsView.qml:428), but no keychain library is linked. Windows Credential Manager caps a credential blob at 2560 bytes ([CREDENTIALA, MS Learn](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/wincred/ns-wincred-credentiala)), and a 21-cookie jar may exceed that. It would need chunking, or a DPAPI-protected file keyed by a small Credential Manager secret.

**macOS:** Qt WebView uses the system WKWebView, but its QML API still cannot enumerate cookies. An Objective-C++ bridge on `WKWebsiteDataStore`/`WKHTTPCookieStore.getAllCookies` would let the Mac session reuse GoogleAccountSheet's flow, the ytcfg harvest JS (SessionBootstrap.swift:161-188) and PoTokenMinter almost unchanged. Google's embedded-browser policy risk still applies there.

**Linux:** Qt WebView uses only WebEngine, which is fine with GCC ([Qt WebView](https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/qtwebview-index.html)).

**Last.fm (nothing to reuse from iOS except the idea of keeping the key out of the repo):** use the desktop auth flow ([last.fm/api/desktopauth](https://www.last.fm/api/desktopauth)):
1. `auth.getToken`.
2. Open `last.fm/api/auth/?api_key=…&token=…` in the system browser.
3. `auth.getSession` returns a session key with infinite lifetime by default.
4. Requests are signed with an MD5 `api_sig` over the sorted parameters plus the shared secret.

The scrobble rule is: the track must be longer than 30s and played for half its length **or 4 minutes, whichever comes first**. Batches hold up to 50, and `track.updateNowPlaying` is sent at start ([last.fm/api/scrobbling](https://www.last.fm/api/scrobbling)). Monolist's step text "once you have heard half of it" (SettingsView.qml:417) leaves out the 4-minute cap and the 30-second minimum.
research.recommendation:
Don't port the iPhone app's embedded-web-view Google sign-in to Windows. It needs a cookie-reading browser that MinGW can't provide. Qt WebEngine doesn't compile with MinGW. Qt WebView can't read cookie values and isn't installed in the local Qt 6.11.2 MinGW kit. Google also blocks sign-in from embedded browsers, and the iOS app only gets through by spoofing the Mobile Safari user agent.

Build the cookie-file route the Settings design already describes:
- **Import:** the user exports a Netscape cookies.txt from a private browser window, following yt-dlp's documented method.
- **Storage:** keep it in chunked or DPAPI-protected secure storage, because a full cookie jar can exceed Credential Manager's 2560-byte limit.
- **yt-dlp:** pass it through a temporary `--cookies` file, and read the file back afterwards to capture rotated cookies.

Reuse the iOS app's hard-won request rules in `innertube.cpp`, written once in C++:
- Scope cookies per host, deduplicate by name with the most specific domain winning, and filter to a browser-like allow-list.
- Build SAPISIDHASH the way yt-dlp does: the user session id from DATASYNC_ID, lowercase hex, and each hash label paired with its own cookie. Send `X-Goog-AuthUser: 0` and `X-Origin`.
- Fetch www.youtube.com with the cookies to get ID_TOKEN, DATASYNC_ID and visitorData.
- Decide signed-in from `logged_in=1` only, and never sign the user out because of a network failure.
- Delete only the auth cookies on sign-out.
- Keep the account read-only.
- Treat the signed-in web_safari HLS request as an optional fallback for networks that block the anonymous lanes, not the main path. Don't send a PO token on it.

On macOS, a small Objective-C++ WKWebView and WKHTTPCookieStore bridge could reuse the iOS login flow almost unchanged, if the owner accepts the user-agent-spoof risk. Build Last.fm fresh with its desktop auth flow in the system browser, and fix the scrobble wording to include the 4-minute cap and the 30-second minimum.
openQuestions: Does Qt 6.11's MinGW distribution ship Qt WebView with the WebView2 backend, and can the WebView2 SDK (WebView2.h / WebView2Loader.dll) be used from MinGW 13? Neither is verified; the local Qt 6.11.2 MinGW kit has no Qt WebView module at all, and installing it would be a download needing approval.

Is the owner willing to ship a user-agent spoof to get around Google's embedded-browser sign-in block (the iOS app does this at GoogleAccountSheet.swift:94-98)? It works against Google's stated policy and could stop working at any time.

Which cookies are HttpOnly (and so invisible to JavaScript `document.cookie`) is from general knowledge, not checked in this session. It matters if anyone considers a Qt WebView plus runJavaScript approach.

Why were the three SAPISIDHASH builders (YouTubeAccountSync, YouTubeAuth, YouTubeSession) left inconsistent on hex case, the `_u` session prefix and cookie scoping? Only the Explore one was validated by AuthDiagnostics. Which behaviour does the owner treat as ground truth?

How the iPhone app handles cookie rotation (__Secure-*PSIDTS, SIDCC) is inferred: API responses never write cookies back, and the hidden www.youtube.com web view probably refreshes the store. Does a static exported cookie file stay valid long enough for Monolist, or must it persist Set-Cookie updates from its own requests?

Is the Last.fm shared secret acceptable to embed in a public MIT desktop build, given a compiled binary exposes it anyway, or should it come from a build-time config kept out of the repo, like the iOS Secrets.plist?

Monolist's Settings text promises 'your library, likes and history' from the account (SettingsView.qml:424, 429). The iPhone app was deliberately read-only and never synced the library or likes (YouTubeAccountSync.swift:11-14). Is library sync actually in scope?
The yt-dlp PO Token Guide says web_safari's HLS formats don't need a GVS PO token 'at this time' (page updated 12 July 2026). This may change and should be rechecked before building on it.

research.findings:
## Where sign-in and scrobbling fit into Monolist's code

Everything here is read-only. I built nothing and changed nothing. I found no `Secrets.plist`, `.env`, cookie or token files anywhere under `\\psf\Home\Desktop\Multiplatform Music player`, so none were opened. Paths below are relative to `\\psf\Home\Desktop\Multiplatform Music player\Monolist Player\`.

---

### 0. How the code works today (the facts the rest depends on)

**InnerTube request building**
- **Client context.** Built in `clientContext()` (`src/innertube.cpp:84-122`):
  - WEB_REMIX uses a version string made from today's date (`:98-101`).
  - WEB is the same idea (`:102-105`).
  - VISIONOS copies the visionOS app's identity exactly (`:106-119`).
- **Headers.** They are all set in one place, `InnerTube::post()` (`src/innertube.cpp:418-446`):
  - Content-Type, User-Agent, Origin and Referer (`:438-441`).
  - `X-Goog-Visitor-Id` and `context.client.visitorData`, only for `Client::Player` (`:429-433`, `:442-443`).
  - There is no `Cookie` or `Authorization` header anywhere.
- **Retries.** `send()` (`:448-499`) retries once on network errors (`:481-487`). It treats **any HTTP 400** as "this country is refused": it clears `g_region` and calls the region-rejected handler (`:470-478`). That handler is wired to `Library::dropRegion`, which wipes the user's chosen country (`src/main.cpp:106-108`).
- **visitorData.** It is scraped from the youtube.com home page with the visionOS user agent (`:371-405`). `player()` waits for it (`:407-416`, `:509`).
- **Region is process-wide state.** `g_region` and `g_regionRejected` are file statics (`:77-79`), set from `main.cpp:105-108`. That pattern fits a signed-in session too.
- **There are six separate `InnerTube` objects, each with its own `QNetworkAccessManager` and cookie jar:**
  - MediaExtractor (`src/mediaextractor.h:114`)
  - Catalog (`src/catalog.h:68`)
  - Lyrics (`src/lyrics.h:110`)
  - Recommender (`src/recommender.h:111`)
  - PlaybackController (`src/playbackcontroller.h:220`)
  - StreamResolver (`src/streamresolver.h:141`)
  
  So a session cannot live in one object's jar; it has to be shared the way the region is.
- **Aside:** every constructor calls `fetchVisitorData()` (`src/innertube.cpp:366`). That is six anonymous youtube.com page fetches at start-up, although only the Player client ever uses the result.

**yt-dlp**
- Every call goes through `YtDlp::run()` (`src/ytdlp.cpp:389-405`), with `commonArguments()` (`:360-387`, including `--ignore-config` at `:363`).
- The calls:
  - `search` (`:407-415`)
  - `resolveAudio` (`:417-428`)
  - `resolveVideo` (`:430-451`)
  - `download` (`:453-530`)
- Arguments go in a `QStringList` through `QProcess`, with no shell (`:76-103`). Adding `--cookies <path>` is mechanically trivial.
- **Logging risk:** after a successful run, the whole stderr is written with qWarning (`:211-212`).

### (a) Last.fm scrobbler

**Rules to implement** (source: https://www.last.fm/api/scrobbling)
- Scrobble only when the track is longer than 30 s **and** has played for half its duration or 4 minutes, whichever comes first.
- Now Playing is optional, sent "as soon as a user starts listening".
- `track.scrobble` accepts up to 50 scrobbles per batch.
- Keep a cache that survives restarts and send it oldest first.
- Error handling:
  - codes 11 and 16: retry
  - code 9: re-authenticate
  - anything else: discard
- Ignored codes 1-5 include "timestamp too far in the past/future" and "max daily scrobbles". The page gives no numbers for these limits.

**Call details**
- `timestamp` is "the time the track started playing", as a UTC Unix time. `chosenByUser` defaults to 1. Both calls are POSTs that need `sk` (https://www.last.fm/api/show/track.scrobble, https://www.last.fm/api/show/track.updateNowPlaying).
- API root is `ws.audioscrobbler.com/2.0/`, and Last.fm asks for an identifiable User-Agent (https://www.last.fm/api/intro). The existing `Monolist/<version>` UA in `src/appinfo.cpp:293-294` can be reused.

**Desktop sign-in** (https://www.last.fm/api/desktopauth, https://www.last.fm/api/show/auth.getSession)
1. Call `auth.getToken`.
2. Open `last.fm/api/auth/?api_key=…&token=…` in the browser with `QDesktopServices::openUrl`, as `src/appinfo.cpp:331-335` already does.
3. Call `auth.getSession`. It returns error 14 ("token not authorized") until the user approves, so it can be polled; error 15 means the token expired (tokens last 60 minutes).
- The session key does not expire.
- `api_sig` is the md5 of the parameters sorted alphabetically, concatenated, with the shared secret appended; `format` and `callback` are excluded and values must be UTF-8 (https://www.last.fm/api/authspec). `QCryptographicHash` in Qt Core is enough.
- No callback server is needed, so Qt HTTP Server and NetworkAuth are not needed (see §c for why that matters).
- This matches the existing copy "password is never typed into this app" (`SettingsView.qml:415`).

**API key and secret in a public MIT repo**
- Strawberry ships a hard-coded key and secret in `lastfmscrobbler.cpp` (https://forum.strawberrymusicplayer.org/topic/5936/last-fm-import-does-not-work-for-large-libraries).
- Last.fm's terms forbid sub-licensing (clause 4.3.3, https://www.last.fm/api/tos). Whether shipping a shared key counts as sub-licensing is **unclear**.
- Suggestion: inject the key and secret at configure time into a generated header in the build tree, mirroring `buildinfo.h.in` / `cmake/buildinfo.cmake` (`CMakeLists.txt:72-93`; `build*/` is git-ignored). Also allow a user-supplied key.
- A desktop binary's secret can always be extracted, so treat it as an identifier, not protection.
